Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old male with a recent insect sting to the arm a few minutes prior, presenting with localized rash and subjective mild breathing difficulty/anxiety; exam and real-time assessment did not show signs of life-threatening allergic reaction.

History:
- Presenting complaint: perceived difficulty breathing and a rash after an insect (bee/wasp) sting to the right arm a few minutes before the consult.
- Timeline:
  - Sting occurred just a few minutes prior to the consult.
  - Symptoms are recent and described as ongoing at time of call; patient reports symptoms are not acutely worsening.
- Local findings at sting site:
  - Puncture mark with slight redness and blotchy rash on right arm.
  - No significant local swelling reported by patient; clinician visualized and described it as appearing “OK” and not particularly swollen.
- Oral/airway symptoms:
  - Patient reports lips feel slightly swollen on the right side and tongue “feels a bit weird.”
  - Patient does not have observable lip swelling on exam; provider visualized mouth/throat and reported no abnormal soft tissue swelling and no signs of airway compromise.
- Respiratory symptoms:
  - Patient reports feeling “some difficulty breathing” but states it is not acute at the moment and appears comfortable while speaking.
  - Clinician observed normal breathing pattern during the consultation and no stridor.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - None specifically identified.
  - No medications taken yet (no antihistamine administered prior to consult).
- Associated symptoms/review of systems:
  - No fever, no signs of systemic anaphylaxis reported or observed.
  - Past history of occasional anxiety/panic attacks (no current medication).
  - No other systemic symptoms mentioned.

Past Medical History:
- Eczema (no further details provided).
- No prior history of anaphylaxis reported.
- No prior prescription of an epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen) reported.

Medications:
- No routine medications documented.
- During consult, oral antihistamines were recommended:
  - Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet — suggested dosing: one tablet (4 mg) up to six times daily.
  - Alternative suggested: “one-a-day” antihistamine (unspecified) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No medications had been taken prior to assessment.

Allergies:
- Penicillin allergy reported.
- No known food or pet allergies reported.

Social History:
- Age: 27 years.
- Occupation: Computer scientist.
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Pets: Has a cat at home.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not documented.
- Financial or lifestyle issues: Not documented.

Family History:
- No relevant family history of acute allergic reactions or other illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- General/airway:
  - Patient speaking normally; breathing observed as appearing adequate.
  - No stridor reported.
- Oropharynx:
  - Clinician visualized mouth/throat; reported no swelling of lips or intraoral soft tissues.
- Skin/local:
  - Right arm: puncture mark with slight redness and a blotchy rash; clinician did not observe significant swelling or signs of severe local reaction.
- No other physical examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp)
  - Assessment: Likely localised reactive redness and mild local inflammation at sting site; no evidence of systemic anaphylaxis or airway compromise at time of evaluation.
  - Plan:
    - Advise oral antihistamine: chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, one tablet up to six times daily as needed for symptoms.
    - Alternative: a once-daily antihistamine (unspecified) if preferred — name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Advice on signs of infection: if redness spreads, area becomes hot or there are signs of localized infection, consider re-evaluation and possible need for antibiotics.
    - Provide patient education materials/links about anaphylactic reactions (as arranged by clinician).
    - Safety-net instruction: return for appointment or attend A&E immediately if symptoms progress (worsening breathing, lip/tongue swelling, stridor, rapid progression).
    - If reaction progresses rapidly, attend A&E rather than wait for a booked appointment.

- Issue 2: Patient anxiety/concern about potential progression
  - Assessment: Patient reports occasional anxiety/panic attacks; current anxiety about possible progression of reaction.
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance provided that current presentation does not appear life-threatening.
    - Encourage low threshold to contact clinician/service for further reassurance or follow-up if worried.

- Issue 3: Penicillin allergy (documented)
  - Assessment: Patient-reported allergy to penicillin; no details on reaction type documented.
  - Plan:
    - Document allergy in medical record; avoid penicillin-class antibiotics if prescribed in future.

General Plan items:
- No allergy testing recommended at this time as this appears to be an isolated, localized reaction.
- Advice to purchase over-the-counter antihistamine from any pharmacy/chemist; no prescription required.
- Follow-up: Patient advised to re-contact service or attend A&E if symptoms worsen.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, temperature) not documented.
  - No detailed medication list or regular meds documented; reconciliation not performed.
  - No description of exact duration since sting in minutes (only “a few minutes ago”), and no photo or measurement of rash size.
  - No further details on nature of penicillin allergy (type of reaction, severity).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient reports subjective lip swelling and tongue “feels a bit weird,” but clinician observed no visible lip or intraoral swelling on examination — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Consultation audio/transcript adequate; clinician instructions and patient responses generally clear and audible.
